articles.title: Destroyed in Operation Sindoor, JeM's Bahawalpur terror base fully operational again
articles.summary: Pakistan News: NEW DELHI: Extensive restoration work has concluded at the Markaz Subhanallah facility, the primary base for the UN-sanctioned terrorist group Jaish-e.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Extensive restoration work has concluded at the Markaz Subhanallah facility, the primary base for the UN-sanctioned terrorist group Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM), a little over a year after the compound suffered severe structural destruction during India's Operation Sindoor retaliatory strikes.Fresh footage indicates it is fully operational again, complete with reconstructed domes, updated interior plastering, new paint, and premium marble flooring that conceals previous blast damage.Deep blast zones within the primary hall were filled with concrete, while ruined satellite buildingsâincluding the Al-Sabir seminary and housing units for leadershipâwere demolished to enable new construction.Intelligence reports indicate that Pakistani authorities channeled 250 million PKR in cash to JeM, with approximately 110 million PKR dedicated specifically to restoring the central complex over a 15-month period.With JeM leader Masood Azhar incapacitated by health issues, day-to-day command of the Bahawalpur facility has shifted to his brothers, Talha Al-Saif and Mohinuddin Aurangzeb (also known as Ammar Alvi).Meanwhile, senior figures Masood Azhar and Rauf Asghar remain harbored under government protection in the Nawabshah district of Sindh, sources said.ALSO READ | Operation Sindoor exposed limits of Pakistan's nuclear deterrenceCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Russia likely to mobilize at least 300,000 more troops to Ukraine war, Zelensky warns
articles.summary: Russia is likely to mobilize another 300,000 troops later this year, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, as it tries to complete the capture of a long-coveted region of east Ukraine.
articles.body: Russia is likely to mobilize another 300,000 troops later this year, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, as it tries to complete the capture of a long-coveted region of east Ukraine. In wide-ranging remarks released Sunday, Zelensky said he expected that the Russians would end the year occupying the same amount of Ukrainian territory as at the beginning of the year, despite enormous losses of manpower. “Russia has lost 267,000 personnel since the start of the year, including around 155,000 killed to date,” Zelensky claimed. The figure is impossible to confirm but in line with estimates by Western officials. Russian parliamentary elections take place next month, and there has been speculation about a fresh mobilization despite a 2022 draft triggering protests and an exodus of young men. “We are confident that following the elections, they will carry out a mobilization. We believe this will not take place in the major cities,” Zelensky said. Zelensky said he believed Putin would “deploy the 300,000 newly mobilized troops depending on the situation in the east of our country,” and had told his generals to complete the occupation of Donetsk by the end of the year. “They’ll lose all 300,000 of these newly mobilized Russians there; we’ll wipe them out,” Zelensky asserted. Ukrainian units are defending some 20% of Donetsk, including a belt of strategic industrial towns such as Slaviansk and Kramatorsk. Zelensky said it was impossible for the Russians to complete the capture of Donetsk region. He suggested the Russians might also attempt an incursion into the northern Ukrainian regions of Kharkiv and Sumy. “They do not yet have troops in the Bryansk region (which borders northern Ukraine), but we can see military equipment along the borders with the Russian Federation.” Musk, Kushner, and air defenses On air defenses, Zelensky contrasted the number of Patriot missiles supplied in 2023 – which was 675 – with the forecast number of 264 this year. Ballistic missile attacks have increased civilian casualties and infrastructure damage across Ukraine - and Patriots are the only means of shooting them down. “As you can see, there is, unfortunately, a downward trend, and this depends primarily on the American side,” he said. Last month, US President Donald Trump suggested Ukraine would be permitted to build Patriot missiles on license, but later backed away from the idea. If the US would supply up to 10% of its Patriot missile stocks to Ukraine, Kyiv would pay for them, Zelensky said. Such a commitment “could make a huge difference, both in terms of saving lives and diplomatically as well.” Ukraine faces the same problem in acquiring Aster air defense missiles from Europe, according to Zelensky, despite a recent pledge by French president Emmanuel Macron. “There aren’t enough ‘Aster’ missiles, even though they are being produced,” he said – though added a licensing agreement would accelerate supplies. Kyiv’s long-range missile program will get a boost Monday when new British Prime Minister Andy Burnham makes his first official visit to Ukraine. London has agreed to allow defense firm MBDA to release classified information on UK components to help Ukraine build its own long-range SCALP missiles, the French-produced version of the UK’s Storm Shadow. In the meantime, Ukraine is hunting the sites in Russia from where ballistic missiles are launched, according to Zelensky. Russia’s military industries may be capable of building about 1,300 ballistic missiles a year, Zelensky said. “There are specific objectives regarding strikes on military targets and other anti-ballistic sanctions,” he said. Ukraine has developed an arsenal of long-range drones and its own cruise missiles which are being used against a widening array of targets inside Russia. He also spoke about Kyiv’s efforts to get permission to use Starlink satellite imagery of Russian territory. Elon Musk, who owns Starlink, said he “believed that this could lead to a major escalation against the Russian Federation on Ukraine’s part,” according to Zelensky. “He said he was in favor of ending the war, not prolonging it” – and discussions with Washington were continuing. As for negotiations, Zelensky suggested that the window of opportunity for ending the war stretched through the end of next summer, when the US presidential election campaign would begin. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were “finding it very difficult to find a format whereby the Russians would agree to end this war without Ukraine having to withdraw from Donbas or accept other unacceptable solutions.” “Jared, Steve and I agreed to summarize all these discussions on a single page – setting out the realistic options for ending the war. This is what the Americans want to discuss with us and with the Russians.”

articles.title: Despite contactless payments, euro banknotes in circulation have risen from about â¬1 trillion in 2016 to â¬1.6 trillion as Europeans keep emergency cash ready for crises and cyber outages
articles.summary: Europe News: Despite the widespread use of contactless payments and smartphones across Europe, people are keeping more physical cash. The value of euro banknotes i.
articles.body: Despite the widespread use of contactless payments and smartphones across Europe, people are keeping more physical cash. The value of euro banknotes in circulation has increased sharply in recent years, as fears over war, cyber-attacks and other emergencies grow.According to European Central Bank (ECB) data, as reported by The Guardian, the total value of euro banknotes in circulation increased from about â¬1 trillion in 2016 to â¬1.6 trillion in June 2026. The number of notes has also increased, with more than 31 billion banknotes now in circulation.The increase comes at a time when cash is used less often for everyday purchases in many European cities. Contactless cards, mobile phones and other digital payment methods have become common. However, people are now keeping cash because they are worried about situations in which digital payment systems may not work.Those concerns include wars, wildfires, floods, storms and cyber-attacks. In such situations, people may not be able to depend on online banking, mobile apps or contactless payment systems. Cash, therefore, can provide a way to pay for basic items when digital systems are unavailable.Why Europeans are keeping cashThe ECB's chief economist, Philip Lane, pointed to the difference between how often cash is used for transactions and how much cash people are holding.âThe total stock of banknotes is continuing to grow. In transactions, the number of notes is coming down, but in terms of the stock, it is increasing,â Lane said, as quoted by The Guradian.This means that even though people may be using fewer banknotes when buying things, the overall amount of physical money being held is rising.The increase has been linked to growing concerns about emergencies. In 2025, people in the European Union were advised to keep enough food, water and other essentials at home to last for 72 hours in case of an emergency.The advice covered possible situations such as wildfires, floods and storms, as well as cyber-attacks and other hostile events. A suggested crisis pack included bottled water, a transistor radio, canned food and cash.A major cyber-attack in the UK last year showed how such disruption can affect businesses.More notes, fewer transactionsECB data has tracked euro banknotes in circulation since 2002. The value of those banknotes has risen from around â¬1 trillion in 2016 to â¬1.6 trillion in June 2026. More than 31 billion banknotes are currently in circulation, compared with 24 billion before the pandemic in 2019.Some European countries have already given people specific advice on how much emergency cash they should keep at home. Austria, Finland, Germany, Sweden and the Netherlands have recommended keeping between â¬70 and â¬100 per household.The suggested amount is intended to cover essential spending for about 72 hours if online and mobile payment services stop working.Cash matters beyond emergenciesOlive McCarthy, a professor at University College Cork who has an interest in financial inclusion, told The Guardian, keeping cash only for emergencies could create another problem.âWhile advice to maintain cash for emergencies is well made, and serves to remind us all to be prepared when digital systems let us down, it is essential that cash does not become viewed merely as a backup measure. If we stop using it when there isnât a crisis, it might not be easy to use it when there is.âMcCarthy also said cash can be important for people who may find digital payments difficult to access. She pointed to elderly and vulnerable people, as well as victims of domestic abuse who may depend on cash if their partner controls their spending. Cash can also help children learn about money, financial literacy and budgeting, she said.The ECB has also pointed to the need to maintain access to cash. Lane referred to the importance of legislation that would ensure cash machines remain available across European high streets.Keeping notes relevantECB is also working on new euro banknotes and prepares for the possible introduction of the digital euro. It unveiled proposals for redesigned euro banknotes in July, Euro News reported. The new designs are expected to use themes connected to European culture and nature, including people who have made contributions to art, music, science and literature, as well as rivers and birds.The central bank has said the redesign is part of its effort to keep banknotes relevant as payment habits change. A public survey is being used to help select the final design, with the winning theme expected to be announced in December 2026. The new notes could enter circulation as late as 2029.The ECB has also stressed that a digital euro would not mean the end of physical cash. Doris Schneeberger, the ECB's banknotes director, said, âWe are committed to ensuring that paying with public money is always an option, be it with cash or with a digital euro. A digital euro would complement cash and not replace it. All Europeans will continue to have the freedom of choice how to pay, be it with cash, the digital euro, or another means of payment.âCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Robots can outrun humans, but can they plug in a cable?
articles.summary: China’s humanoid robots have ​shown they can run quicker than the fastest humans.
articles.body: China’s humanoid robots have ​shown they can run quicker than the fastest humans. Now comes the real test: Can they also handle packaging ‌and warehouse operations while reliably performing precision tasks like connecting cables designed to evaluate their ability to work like humans in less flashy jobs? The five-day World Humanoid Robot Games, which began Saturday in Beijing, combine events modeled on human sports with those designed to test the robots in simulated factories, restaurants and ​offices and in emergency situations. The games, heavily promoted in Chinese state media, feature 51 events, including 30 sports competitions and ​21 scenario-based contests. More than 40% require robots to operate fully autonomously, according to Huawei, a tech ⁠partner of the games. On Saturday, two robots ran faster than Usain Bolt’s 9.58-second world record in the 100-meter sprint. That was a ​sharp improvement from 2025, when the winning robot’s time was more than 20 seconds. Braking was an issue, as the machines slammed into ​a thick mat that organizers placed several feet after the finish line. Another humanoid, the same model as the 100-meter champion, ran 400 meters in 39.7 seconds, faster than South African Wayde van Niekerk’s world record of 43.03 seconds. “The intensity is higher than last year, which places significant demands on the robot’s ​battery management and thermal dissipation capabilities,” said spectator and robotics investor Xu Qiaosheng. “It holds huge significance for the development of China’s industrial ​sector.” Robots will compete in tug-of-war and weightlifting, while tai chi and pitch-pot — in which contestants throw arrow-like sticks into a narrow-necked vase — will give traditional ‌Chinese ⁠sports a futuristic twist. Beyond the spectacle, the more revealing tests could come when robots encounter the small imperfections of the physical world: a cable at the wrong angle, an object just out of reach, a shifting package or a missed step. That tests whether robots can identify objects, accurately position their hands and bodies, apply controlled force and recover from errors without human intervention. Lumos Robotics ​Chief Executive Yu Chao said ​the games could help improve ⁠hardware and provide a showcase for the industry. But Yu said the longer-term value will depend on real-world problem solving. “Only when it can work in those end scenarios does it have real value,” Yu ​said. “Simply running and jumping does not improve efficiency.” In addition to more familiar events drawn from human ​sports, robots will ⁠compete in EV charging, restaurant work, emergency incident handling and hand-dexterity contests. There are also industrial assembly and material loading events. A cable connection challenge is a test of vision, mechanical alignment and force control. Beijing-based robotics startup Galbot said it would stage an autonomous humanoid tennis match, ⁠with robots ​attempting singles and doubles play, including ball tracking, serving and returning shots. For Hua ​Rong, chief marketing officer at robotics firm Zeroth, the real test will come after the demonstrations end. “The competition will be whether, after the product is sold, it can ​really solve users’ problems,” she said.

articles.title: France links sharp rise in drownings to prolonged heatwaves
articles.summary: A government minister says people have been taking risks by going into the water, with 301 deaths since 19 June.
articles.body:
France has seen 301 drownings since 19 June, a government minister has said, linking the sharp rise in deaths from last year to a series of prolonged heatwaves.

Sports and Youth Minister Marina Ferrari told France Inter radio the number of deaths - a 14% hike on 2025 - was a "tragic toll".

France, Spain and Italy have all been hit by heatwaves that have triggered massive wildfires that have scorched thousands of hectares of land this summer.

Ferrari said people had been taking risks by going into the water, adding: "Many deadly accidents have occurred in areas that are not authorised or supervised for swimming."

She said a number of the drownings were recorded in "open water, in canals for example".

Ferrari said the government was working with regional authorities "to improve swimming areas and make things safer".

Speaking on Friday, she added that "many drownings, particularly among the elderly, occurred in individual pools".

The minister said that sudden immersion in cold water on a hot day could cause shock, and that in some cases "people can also exceed their physical capabilities".

In June, Ferrari warned that too many people were trying to cool off in rivers and canals without necessarily taking the risks into account.

Climate change is driving up global average temperatures, making heatwaves more frequent and intense.

This has been felt acutely in Europe, which is the fastest warming continent, heating up twice as fast as the global average, according to the Copernicus climate service. , external

Drowning deaths soar in France as Europe buckles in peak of heatwave Published 23 June

Drowning deaths soar in France as Europe buckles in peak of heatwave

A heatwave in June saw a nuclear power plant in south-west France temporarily shut down because water temperatures in the River Garonne topped 28C. Under French laws, water used to cool the reactors at the Golfech plant must not exceed that temperature.

Some monuments like the Eiffel Tower also decided to close early because of the high temperatures in Paris during the heatwave.

The dry conditions also saw wildfires spread across France, with Gironde, around the city of Bordeaux in the south-west of the country, being the worse affected area, with more than 200,000 people being forced from their homes in late July.

France has logged 7,300 excess deaths between late May and 22 July, according to provisional figures from the public health authorities.

articles.title: âEntering endgameâ: US turns to âeconomic D-Dayâ against Iran; Tehran raises Gulf oil blockade threat
articles.summary: Middle East News: The United States is set for what Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has described as the âgreatest financial offensive ever marshalledâ against Iran, w.
articles.body: The United States is set for what Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has described as the âgreatest financial offensive ever marshalledâ against Iran, with new sanctions expected to target countries and businesses that continue trading with Tehran."President Trump has dismantled Iranâs military capabilities, destroyed nearly 100 percent of its military factories, and buried its nuclear program. We are now entering the endgame. At dawn begins an economic D-Day â the single greatest financial offensive ever marshaled against an adversary," said Bessent in a post on X."The Islamic Republic has subsisted by dressing extortion as security guarantees. It has drawn strength from a calculus that regards Iranian retaliation as certain and American enforcement as negotiable. Under President Trump, that era is over. And those who fear the danger of defying Tehran ought not to discount the cost of testing Washington," he added.Further continuing the threat against Iran, the treasury secretary warned, "The President has created the conditions to leverage every agency, every authority and action many assumed we would never summon. Our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains the tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone."Bessent is also set to hold a press conference at 2 pm EDT (1800 GMT) on Monday, when he is expected to outline the new measures. In an opinion article published in the Financial Times on Sunday, he said the US would target countries that engage with Iranâs economy and financial system despite Washingtonâs pressure.âThey would do well to consider the consequences of sustaining it,â Bessent wrote, referring to countries he accused of practising âappeasementâ towards Tehran.Iran has responded with a threat of its own, warning that it could halt all oil exports from the Persian Gulf if Washington continues what it called an âeconomic warâ.The escalation comes even as direct military action between the US and Iran has paused. The two sides have not exchanged major strikes for weeks, but neither has returned to meaningful negotiations to end the six-month-old conflict.Oil and Hormuz in the crosshairsIranian officials have warned that economic pressure could trigger a wider confrontation in the Gulf.Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iranâs Supreme National Security Council, said on Sunday that Iran could stop oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz and from elsewhere in the Persian Gulf if the sanctions campaign continued. He also warned that Tehran would consider any country supporting the US economic offensive to be participating in an âact of warâ.The threat carries global implications. Iran has retained missile and drone capabilities that could threaten Gulf states and shipping, while disruption in the Strait of Hormuz has already brought tanker traffic through the key waterway close to a standstill and pushed up global fuel prices.Bessent has also called on China to cooperate with the US, pointing to its dependence on Gulf oil for roughly half of its imports.Beijing has rejected the pressure campaign. A spokesperson for the Chinese embassy in Washington said sanctions and pressure would not resolve the dispute and called for diplomacy instead.The new measures would hit an Iranian economy already weakened by years of sanctions, high inflation, a falling currency, energy shortages and structural problems.The latest escalation also comes as efforts to revive negotiations remain limited. The last direct US-Iran talks took place in Switzerland in June, with Qatar, Pakistan and Turkey since trying to mediate.Pakistan said its army chief, Asim Munir, would visit Tehran on Monday as part of efforts to restore regional peace and security. A Pakistani government source said the US threat of fresh sanctions would be among the issues discussed.The diplomatic efforts come against a backdrop of continued uncertainty over Iranâs nuclear programme, which Washington and Israel have sought to dismantle.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: There's a renewed crackdown on how Iranian women dress
articles.summary: Four years after the death of Mahsa Amini, and the "Women, Life, Freedom" protests that followed, it seems the way Iranian women dress is back in the spotlight. As the US-Iran war stalls, videos circulating on social media show women being shamed on the streets for what they're wearing, particularly if they don't have the mandatory hijab on. CNN's Jomana Karadsheh reports.

articles.title: Divorce, smartphones and control - BBC sees how Taliban run Afghanistan
articles.summary: Five years after the Taliban’s return, the BBC follows senior figures as the group reshapes the country.
articles.body:
Governor Abdullah Sarhadi gives money to treat a boy's broken arm and hands out funds for a local mosque - then, in his office in northern Afghanistan, an astonishing exchange unfolds.

A young woman tells the grey-bearded former Taliban commander that she wants to divorce her husband, who she accuses of months of abuse and beatings.

In a country where girls are banned from secondary education, the 18-year-old argues her case calmly and confidently, her face completely hidden behind a full-face veil and sunglasses.

"If there was any chance to live together, I wouldn't be here… I have taken my decision," she says.

After trying to persuade her to avoid divorce, the governor later comments that women are "mindless" and "deficient in intellect", to laughter from the male officials, bodyguards and elders around him.

The moment gives a rare glimpse into the day-to-day realities of the Taliban's rule, five years after they swept aside the US-backed government in 2021.

In that time, women have been excluded from most workplaces, banned from universities and may not travel alone or visit parks and leisure centres.

In encounters spread over two years, the BBC gained unusual access to influential figures in the extreme Islamist movement, spending time with men who once planned suicide attacks or spent years in underground hideouts, but are now officials and soldiers.

The Taliban came into power saying they had changed, but many of their policies are similar to the hard-line interpretation of Sharia - Islamic religious law - they imposed in the 1990s.

The men we met seemed to want to present themselves as reasonable, yet were not keen to discuss their past violence. And we saw moments of unease between the rulers and those they rule.

Afghan women tell the BBC their lives are unrecognisable after five years of Taliban rule

Five years of the BBC questioning the Taliban over women and girls' education

Governor Sarhadi says Tuba – not her real name – should stay in the marriage.

"Ask yourself: 'Who would marry me after I get my divorce?'" says Sarhadi. "You'll have to compromise a lot or you'll lose your dignity and honour."

"Mr Governor, my honour and dignity have already been ruined," she responds.

Her husband listens, awaiting his turn to speak.

Under Sharia, a woman requesting that her husband agrees to a divorce may have to return some or all of the money given to her by him when they married. A financial settlement is often agreed. But this woman's husband says he wants four times the amount, which her family refuses to pay.

The governor says the woman should be given her own room. He adds that officials will warn him not to beat her - "otherwise he'd be jailed".

Unsatisfied, Tuba's father later tells the BBC the family will pursue divorce through the courts, even though, under the Taliban's court system, it is very difficult for a woman to get a divorce without the husband's consent.

Sarhadi was a military commander during the Taliban's first stint in power in the 1990s. He was among thousands of insurgents who surrendered in late 2001 as a US-led coalition ousted the group.

He was held for several years in US detention in Guantanamo Bay, but eventually released.

When the Taliban regained power, he became a governor - first in the province of Bamiyan, then when we met him in late June, in Sheberghan city in Jawzjan province. He has recently become deputy commander of a military corps in the northern province of Kunduz.

Tapping on an old-style mobile with a tiny screen, he says a recent ban on smartphones for officials has slowed things down. "Before, you could send a quick message… sending documents and getting an answer fast." If he says any more about the ban, "it will cause trouble", he adds.

But in other ways his worldview seems largely unchanged from the Taliban's position 25 years ago. Then, he was a military commander in Bamiyan, where the Taliban blew up ancient giant Buddha statues, triggering international shock and condemnation.

He initially tries to avoid our questions about the archaeological site, but eventually, he says: "I destroyed it with my own hands.

"Whatever we did and we do is in accordance with the guidance and God's law… We smash idols rather than sell them. Why should I regret? It was God's will."

In the capital Kabul, we meet another senior Taliban figure who swapped a violent past for a role with the ruling administration.

Habibullah Badr drives us through the streets in an armoured car.

He says he was previously "responsible for the operations of suicide attackers" in Kabul.

"I know all the roads and streets very well… we had all the information we needed about Kabul and its alleys," he says. "There were areas that needed a long time to plan."

Taliban suicide attacks killed thousands of people in Afghanistan, including many civilians.

Badr is cautious about discussing his past though, fearing it will "make people upset" and could "reopen wounds".

Asked about civilian deaths, he says the Taliban targeted US convoys and that civilians were urged to stay away from foreign bases.

Whenever I try to ask him about specific attacks that took place in civilian areas, he evades the question.

He is currently taking time out from official roles for medical treatment, but was previously deputy head of prisons for the whole country – and ran the very jail where he was held on death row under the previous government.

Badr invites us to join him at a tribal gathering, where the head of a charitable foundation is to honour him with a medal. But things take an unexpected turn.

"Mr Badr is a pride for Afghanistan and a great fighter," says Sultan Mohammad Talaee. "But I also have a complaint. If the schools and education were open to all it would be a great work for Afghanistan. I hope this doesn't offend you."

An awkward silence follows, his audience unsure how to react. Talaee's microphone is swiftly removed.

Afterwards, he tells the BBC: "I requested for the girls' schools to reopen… seeking knowledge is an obligation for both men and women in Islam."

He adds: "There were other things I wanted to say but they didn't let me talk more."

Often those who speak out face much more severe consequences.

Women told us of the deep despair they felt over dreams thwarted by restrictions on education, and of friends jailed for protesting.

Most journalists we spoke to said they had been summoned or questioned by the Taliban's intelligence organisation, Estikhbaraat.

The BBC put some of these concerns to the Taliban government's spokesman, known as Zabihullah Mujahid.

He has been a public face for the Taliban government since 2021. He still uses the pseudonym he went by for years during the insurgency, but he told us his real name is Tahir Shah Seddiqi - revealing it publicly for the first time.

In a lavish press centre funded by the Americans for the previous government, we ask him about the first press conference he gave there, two days after the Taliban took control of the country.

Then, he told the world the Taliban government would allow women to work and study "within our frameworks" and they would "be very active" in society. Why did they fail to keep their word?

"We are committed to women's rights, freedom of speech and other things within Sharia," he replies. "We should see everything through the Sharia lens."

Allowing women to work in offices such as his own "would lead to immoralities" and "their dignity would be undermined", he adds.

He says the issue of education for women is "under discussions… we need a Sharia-based solution for it".

When questioned about the Taliban's crackdown on media freedom, he says: "In a society like Afghanistan we have our restrictions. We can't let media do whatever propaganda they want… they can't broadcast against Islamic laws and rites."

The Taliban government sits in Kabul, but Mujahid spends a lot of time in the southern city of Kandahar, the Taliban's heartland, which some now consider the de facto capital.

We ask to meet the Taliban's supreme leader, Hibatullah Akhundzada, who is based there. He rarely appears in public and has never given a media interview - we are told it will not be possible at the moment.

Restrictions have been tightened in Kandahar since I last visited two years ago. Now men must have beards. Radio stations are not allowed to play music or broadcast women's voices, and we were not allowed to film in the city.

Two hours' drive away, along dusty roads, some of the group's most devoted former fighters showed the BBC the insurgents' old secret cave network.

Abid Lalai, a former fighter who now mans a checkpoint as part of a security force under the interior ministry, shows us the holes he fired from and the places he used to put his Quran and hang AK-47s.

His superior, Abdul Samad, shows us an unmarked graveyard, saying his father is buried here, killed fighting for the Taliban.

The area is one of the most deprived in a country where the UN says three in four people cannot provide for their basic needs. Samad says the local population desperately need water, roads and clinics.

"Emirate [Taliban] officials have not forgotten us," says Samad. He says the leaders may be busy with other priorities. "We are hopeful, they will look after us sometime."

Five years since the Taliban began their second stint in power, poverty, unemployment and economic instability remain pressing concerns.

Taliban figures we spoke to said they were working to tackle them, but we met other people who believe the group itself is the country's main problem.

"I'm speechless about how a group that has no understanding about life is suddenly in power," says Hoda - not her real name - a woman who protested on the streets when the Taliban first returned to power.

"Women can't accept this situation," she tells the BBC. "They might advance restrictions but it won't stay like this forever."

"I think the Taliban are scared of educated women," she adds. "That's why they restrict women. They want uneducated women so they can't raise wise men. Because that would end the Taliban."

Additional reporting by Hafizullah Maroof

articles.title: After Australia, New Zealand proposes social media ban for under 16
articles.summary: Rest of World News: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon unveiled a proposed law on Monday that would ban children under 16 from using social media platforms, cit.
articles.body: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon unveiled a proposed law on Monday that would ban children under 16 from using social media platforms, citing concerns over the impact of social media on young people.Luxon said that his party would introduce the bill in Parliament, with social media platforms facing fines of up to 10 per cent of their global revenue if they fail to comply.âWe simply cannot accept the harm being done to a generation of New Zealand childrenâ, he said in a statement.The proposal would cover platforms including Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat and Facebook.However, as per AFP, messaging platforms such as WhatsApp, online gaming platforms like Roblox and AI applications with productivity uses, including ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot, would be excluded.According to Luxon, social media was exposing children to harmful content, addictive technology and pressures they were not equipped to deal with, affecting their family life, mental health, sleep and education.However, AFP reported that the proposal does not currently have enough support to pass through Parliament. Two of the three parties in Luxonâs coalition government, libertarian ACT and New Zealand First, have said they will vote against it.Hence, Luxton may require some support from lawmakers in the opposition.New Zealand First leader and foreign minister, Winston Peters, said his party was concerned about the proposed legislation and the direction it could take the country. He described Australiaâs social media ban as a âcolossal failureâ and said keeping children off social media should be the responsibility of parents.In December 2025, Australia became the first country to ban social media for children under 16. Reuters reported that the Australian law blocked children from platforms including TikTok, YouTube, Instagram and Facebook.Since then, countries including Canada, Brazil and Indonesia have also enacted bans, while several other countries are considering or developing similar laws.Luxonâs government also introduced a ban in 2024 on students of all ages using mobile phones during the school day.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Trump tightens Iran squeeze, hurting China and India in the process
articles.summary: Middle East News: The TOI correspondent from Washington: As the war against Iran drags on, the Trump administration on Monday announced an effort intended to cut Tehran.
articles.body: The TOI correspondent from Washington: As the war against Iran drags on, the Trump administration on Monday announced an effort intended to cut Tehran off from the global economy. Treasury secretary Scott Bessent said, âWe are launching an economic onslaught against Iranâs financial connections around the globe. Our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone. We are going to hold everyone accountable, and this is economic asphyxiation of this regime.âHe added that countries not joining US sanctions would âshare in the isolationâ of Iran, and noted that Trump is making phone calls to world leaders with requests to stop their interactions with Tehran.The US treasury department has mapped the networks, facilitators and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil and evade sanctions and said that Washington would be working with US partners to target any source of Iranâs âillicit revenueâ. The department said it has issued determinations againÂ­st five sectors â digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping â that the Iranian govt is using to prop up its economy. The treasury has also imÂ­posed sanctions on nearly 60 entities, individuals and vessels.âAt dawn begins an economic D-Day â the single greatest financial offensive ever mÂ­aÂ­rshalled against an adversary,â Bessent wrote in the FinaÂ­ncial Times, revealing that TrÂ­uÂ­mp had created the condiÂ­tiÂ­ons for Washington to use âevÂ­ery agency, every authorityâ available to isolate Iran and sever âevery economic lifelineâ sustaining the Iranian regime.For New Delhi, the immediate concern is trade rather than strategic alignment. Indian exports of rice, tea and pharmaceuticals to Iran have increasingly moved through Dubai, and UAEâs restrictions combined with tougher US sanctions could severely disrupt those flows. Bilateral trade has already fallen more than 90% from its 2018-19 peak of about $17 billion.Also read: India was wary of Trumpâs âunpredictable behaviourâ, chose no joint presser with PM Modi: ReportChina will be the bigger test for Washington. Beijing is Iranâs principal oil customer and has continued buying discounted Iranian crude through independent refineries and opaque shipping and payment networks. Iranian shipments to China fell to about 534,000 barrels a day in Aug from 823,000 in July, but flows have remained substantial. Bessent has warned Beijing that cooperation would be in its own interest, but China has rejected unilateral sanctions, saying that they âdo not help resolve the problemâ. Asked MoÂ­nday if Chinese banks dealing with Iran could be targeted, Bessent said, âno one is above the reach of US sanctionsâ.The administration has already imposed layers of sanctions on Iranian oil, shipping, banks and companies and has used a naval blockade to disrupt Iranian petroleum exports. Bessent described the new strategy as a âone-two punchâ: âWe have the blockade ... and we are going to have the toughest sanctions in history,â he said, adding the aim was to âcollapse this regimeâ.What makes Mondayâs announcement different is therefore enforcement and reach. Washington will target the third-country networks through which Iran has continued to sell oil, move money and obtain goods despite decades of sanctions. The message is essentially: doing business with Tehran will increasingly mean choosing between access to Iran and access to the US-dominated financial system.Tehran has responded with a threat that could make the economic offensive a global energy crisis. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iranâs supreme national security council, warned that if the âeconomic warâ continues, ânot a single drop of oil will be exportedâ from the Persian Gulf. UAE has already halted much of its trade with Iran, while Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait and Bahrain face the risk that Iranian retaliation could hit ports, shipping, energy infrastructure or trade routes.Iranâs rial hits new record lowIranâs currency hit a record low Monday as Washington annouÂ­ncÂ­ed new sanctions. The rial dropped to 2.02 million to the US dollar as trading opened on currency markets. Iranâs official Central Bank rate stood at around 1.5 million rial to the dollar, but the market rate is what most Iranians pay. Iran currency has repeatedly hit new loÂ­ws as nearly six months of war have taken an even greater toll. IranÂ­ians find daily staples increasingly unaffordable. Since the war begÂ­an, rice is up some 60% and prices of beef are more than 150% highÂ­er. The IMF forecasts that GDP will contract more than 5%.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Trump inauguration pastor says Dearborn Christians 'afraid' to speak out in Muslim-majority city
articles.summary: Lorenzo Sewell says Christians in Dearborn, Michigan, privately told him they are afraid to express their faith, accusing city officials of upholding Sharia law.
articles.body: A Detroit pastor who delivered a prayer at President Donald Trump’s inauguration says Christians in Muslim-majority Dearborn, Michigan, have privately told him they are afraid to publicly express their faith, while accusing local officials of giving Muslim residents preferential treatment under a "two-tiered justice system." "Right now, the city officials in Dearborn specifically, they are giving Muslims preferential treatment," Lorenzo Sewell, senior pastor of 180 Church in Detroit, told Fox News Digital in an interview Monday. "Now, how do I know that?" Sewell asked. "This is how I know that. Being a Black man in the city of Detroit, we go to Dearborn. We know that the police know how to enact justice in Dearborn. They know how to pull you over. They know that if they catch you shoplifting, we've had Black women that tried to elude the police and lost their lives in the city of Dearborn." GOP LAWMAKERS URGE SUPREME COURT TO STRENGTHEN FIRST AMENDMENT PROTECTIONS FOR STREET PREACHERS "So, as a Black man that has grown up around Arabs my entire life, I know that the Dearborn police can enact justice," he continued. "So, when someone is being assaulted and nothing happens, when someone's being assaulted and the police choose to look the other way, you can see clearly a two-tiered justice system."  "So, the city council, instead of them renouncing Sharia law, they are actually upholding Sharia law," Sewell added. Sewell recently went viral following remarks he gave at a Dearborn town hall where he said, "America, we have lost this city. This is a city that is no longer up under American laws; we are up under Sharia law. We will not have it anymore." FORT WORTH PRINCIPAL PICK FACES BACKLASH, INVESTIGATION OVER SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS DEFENDING SHARIA LAW CBS News reported last Wednesday that Dearborn police said they made 22 arrests following the "Christian Crusader March," led by conservative activist Jake Lang. Sewell attended the march, which took place near a regularly scheduled Dearborn City Council meeting where he later delivered his viral remarks. In a statement, Dearborn Police Chief Issa Shahin said, "Our officers met a challenging and rapidly evolving situation with the professionalism this community expects, keeping everyone safe, protecting the constitutional rights of those who came to be heard, and allowing the City Council to complete its business. I could not be prouder of them." DOJ WEIGHS CIVIL RIGHTS PROBE INTO FORT WORTH POLICE OVER ALLEGED FIRST AMENDMENT VIOLATIONS Sewell told Fox News Digital he is concerned about the growing presence of what he called Sharia law practices in the community. "One of the examples that I see of Sharia law happening right here in the metro Detroit … in the city of Hamtramck, you are allowed right now to sacrifice animals, literally," Sewell said. "Number two, halal meat. If you go to a public school, you are literally eating meat that's sacrificed to idols, because, according to Sharia law, that's what — that's a lawful meat."  "And I believe the most concerning to me is the call to prayer," he added. "There is no other place in the world that you can go and tell that country, although you are a majority Christian country, you can't go anywhere else in the nation and tell that country they have to change the way they express their religious beliefs." CALIFORNIA LAWMAKERS' PUSH TO MAKE MUSLIM HOLY DAYS STATE HOLIDAYS SPARKS DEBATE OVER SCHOOL NEUTRALITY In January 2023, the Hamtramck City Council voted to allow animal sacrifice, and the website for Dearborn Public Schools says, "Dearborn Public Schools ensures all meats served in our schools are certified Halal." The certificate for the halal meat, partially in Arabic, reads in part, "We certify that the food processing facility of Saad Wholesale, Inc. in Detroit, MI, USA has been inspected and approved by our Islamic organization for processing, packing, and labeling of Halal Meat & Poultry Products by applying our procedures according to the Islamic Rites." "I see the city council upholding Sharia law through things like the call to prayer, through things like halal meat, through having more Arab writing than they do actually English, by having the chief of police talk more about protecting the rules of Islam and Islamic leaders instead of protecting the rights of all Americans," Sewell continued. "So you can see clearly when someone speaks freely, they can be attacked, and it'd be justified," he added. "I can give you a clear example. My wife had her life threatened. We had the guy's number, we had his address, we had everything, and the lieutenant did absolutely nothing. So, that's how you can see a two-tier justice system." DEI HIRING BOOST FOR ONE BLUE STATE'S MUSLIM COMMISSION INITIATIVE FLIES IN FACE OF TRUMP'S ANTI-WOKE PUSH He also claimed that Christians in the area feel afraid to express their faith. "Since I went viral, I've had Dearborn Christians come out from the north, south, east, and west, and they're afraid," Sewell said. "I want you to think about this for a moment, America. Think about being in a Christian nation, being afraid to talk about Christ. I want you to just think about that for a moment." "I'm having people say, 'I'm with you, but I'm afraid to say it,'" he continued. "'I'm with you, but I'm afraid to be by you.' 'I'm with you —' This is how we know we are in a two-tiered system because, in a Christian nation, we're afraid to be Christians." TRUMP DOJ EXPANDS RELIGIOUS LIBERTY PROTECTIONS AFTER MAJOR SUPREME COURT RULINGS Dearborn city council president Mike Sareini told Fox News Digital that the pastor’s claims are false. "The City of Dearborn is an American city governed by the U.S. Constitution, the laws of the State of Michigan, and the City of Dearborn Charter," Sareini said. "Those laws apply equally to every resident, regardless of religion or background. Everyone is treated the same." "There is no evidence of preferential treatment for any religious group. These accusations are unfounded, and I challenge anyone to present evidence otherwise," Sareini continued. "Dearborn is home to approximately 30 churches and 10 mosques," he added. "Most recently, pastors from throughout Dearborn spoke at a press conference and publicly confirmed that people of different faiths live together peacefully in Dearborn, without the conflict being alleged." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital reached out to Dearborn mayor Abdullah Hammoud and the Dearborn Police Department for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

articles.title: Quaest: veja números da disputa presidencial em MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa divulgada nesta terça-feira (25) foi encomendada pela Rede Matogrossense de Comunicação (RMC). Margem de erro é de três pontos percentuais.
articles.summary: Pesquisa divulgada nesta terça-feira (25) foi encomendada pela  Rede Matogrossense de Comunicação (RMC). Margem de erro é de três pontos percentuais.
articles.body:
Candidatos à Presidência da República em 2026 — Foto: Montagem/g1

Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta terça-feira (25) mostra como está a disputa pela Presidência da República no 1º turno entre os eleitores de Mato Grosso. O levantamento foi encomendado pela Rede Matogrossense de Comunicação (RMC).

Veja, abaixo, os resultados da pesquisa estimulada, em que a Quaest mostra a lista de candidatos aos eleitores entrevistados. A lista inclui Pablo Marçal (PRTB), que registrou candidatura apesar de estar inelegível. O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) vai julgar se ele está apto a concorrer.

✅ Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 MT no WhatsApp

Veja, primeiro, o cenário sem Pablo Marçal.

Veterinário Wilson Grassi (Democrata): 0%

Veja, agora, o cenário com Pablo Marçal.

Quaest em MT: Wellington Fagundes, 27%; Otaviano Pivetta, 23%; Doutora Natasha, 8%; Sargento Laudicério, 2%

Quaest para o Senado em MT: Mauro Mendes (União) tem 24%; Janaína Riva (MDB), 18%; Pedro Taques (PSB), 8%

Para 78% dos eleitores ouvidos no levantamento, a escolha do candidato é definitiva. Outros 22% dizem que ainda podem mudar o voto até as eleições, em 4 de outubro.

A Quaest ouviu 804 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais entre os dias 21 e 24 de agosto. A margem de erro é de três pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos, e o nível de confiança é de 95%. O número de registro no TSE é MT-04846/2026 e BR-00817/2026.

articles.title: Megaigreja tem tecnologia de estádio, lago de batismo e até cafeteria | G1
articles.standfirst: Estrutura com três templos está localizada em uma área de quase 30 mil metros quadrados ao lado do Aeroporto de Vitória e é uma das maiores da América Latina, segundo a administração.
articles.summary: Estrutura com três templos está localizada em uma área de quase 30 mil metros quadrados ao lado do Aeroporto de Vitória e é uma das maiores da América Latina, diz a administração.
articles.body:
Três templos, capacidade para receber até 12 mil pessoas de forma simultânea, fragrância exclusiva e equipamentos usados em estádios de futebol e até no Rock in Rio: a Assembleia de Deus Fonte de Vida inaugurou, neste domingo (23), um novo megacampus em Vitória .

A área, de quase 30 mil metros quadrados, também inclui restaurante, livraria, lago artificial para batismo e é uma das maiores estruturas eclesiásticas da América Latina, segundo a administração.

📲 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 ES no WhatsApp

Pejota, gestor de comunicação da igreja, que fica ao lado do Aeroporto de Vitória, afirmou que a obra foi realizada com recursos próprios no terreno da Zurich Airport Brasil, administradora do aeroporto.

"O terreno não é nosso, a Zurich continua como administradora. É uma concessão. Todo caixa da igreja é feito de dízimos e ofertas, 60% desse caixa é revertido em campo missionário. Um trabalho que não parou mesmo com a construção do campus", explicou o gestor, que não deu detalhes sobre os valores envolvidos na construção.

Megaigreja para 12 mil pessoas com fragrância exclusiva no ES: compare o complexo religioso com outros grandes templos do Brasil

"Os membros da igreja têm noção dos custos da obra, a gente é muito transparente com isso. Mas isso não é algo que a gente queira divulgar para a mídia", completou.

Ao g1 , a Zurich Airport Brasil informou que a área foi disponibilizada por meio de uma cessão onerosa de uso, modalidade pela qual o ocupante paga mensalmente pela utilização do terreno . "Esse modelo é amplamente utilizado na gestão de áreas concedidos e está em conformidade com a legislação e os contratos que regem as concessões aeroportuárias", explicou a administradora.

A construção do campus teve início em 2024 e, segundo a igreja, envolveu mais de mil pessoas. São três templos, com capacidade para 10 mil fiéis: um principal, para 6 mil pessoas; um secundário, para 2 mil,;e um terceiro dedicado ao público infantil, também para 2 mil lugares.

Somando os outros espaços, a expectativa da administração é receber até 12 mil pessoas simultaneamente.

Megacampus da Assembleia de Deus Fonte de Vida foi inaugurado em Vitória — Foto: Divulgação

Tecnologia de ponta e 'experiências sensoriais'

A estrutura conta ainda com restaurante, cafeteria, livraria, oito salas de reunião e um lago artificial externo com arquibancada.

"Somos hoje a maior igreja do estado e uma das maiores igrejas da América Latina. Além dos templos, há ainda espaço para em torno de 2 mil pessoas caminhando no foyer. Nós estamos projetando receber aqui 12 mil pessoas", afirmou o pastor presidente Delano Maia Dos Santos.

Para além da megaestrutura, o espaço também reúne tecnologias e "experiências sensoriais" de alto padrão. Nos templos, são usados painéis de LED multilíngues, mega telão, iluminação de espetáculo e uma câmera "spidercam" — modelo usado para fazer imagens aéreas de jogos de futebol.

Mata Atlântica que cerca o Convento da Penha revela diversidade de espécies em meio à fé dos devotos

Fé que sustenta: Festa da Penha movimenta turismo e transforma rotina de empreendedores

Templo da Assembleia de Deus Fonte de Vida — Foto: Divulgação

A sonorização do espaço é feita com equipamentos usados na Ópera de Viena e inclui uma mesa de som igual a utilizada no festival Rock in Rio.

"A única igreja no mundo que tem uma Spidercam comprada é a Fonte de Vida. São nove câmeras só no templo. Já a sonorização é a mesma que está sendo usada agora no Teatro de Viena, a L-Acoustics. Não tem nenhuma igreja na América Latina com o som L-Acoustics, é o melhor do mundo. A nossa mesa de som é a DiGiCo, a que roda o Rock in Rio", completou o pastor.

Na cafeteria do campus, fiéis têm acesso a um café exclusivo da Fonte de Vida, à venda apenas no local. Há, ainda, uma fragrância exclusiva que perfuma os templos e é oferecida de forma gratuita a quem visitar a igreja pela primeira vez.

"O lema da Gestão de Experiência é provai e vede que o Senhor é bom, do Salmo 34:8. A pessoa teve uma experiência com Jesus, provou Jesus, que é bom, que ama, perdoa. Então tudo é pensado para que as pessoas conheçam Jesus", disse o pastor Delano.

Assembleia de Deus Fonte de Vida tem café e fragrância exclusivos — Foto: Divulgação

Igreja reúne 11 mil membros no Espírito Santo

A Assembleia de Deus Fonte de Vida foi inaugurada em 2006, na garagem de uma residência em Vitória. Onze anos depois, a igreja passou a funcionar em um templo na Mata da Praia, também na capital.

Segundo a administração, hoje são 6 mil membros no campus sede do aeroporto e mais 5 mil em outros municípios capixabas. A Fonte de Vida é também a base do movimento Legendários no Espírito Santo, com mais de 3 mil participantes, e sustenta missionários em diferentes países.

Veja FOTOS do megacampus da Assembleia de Deus Fonte de Vida

O pastor presidente afirma que, apesar da estrutura, a igreja mantém seu compromisso espiritual.

“Mesmo sem ter nada, a gente era excelente na adoração a Deus. Tínhamos uma boa Palavra, que é o fundamental, porque se você tem uma excelência estrutural e tem uma pobreza espiritual, você perde a identidade do que ser. Deus é excelente em tudo o que Ele faz, e a maior prova disso é que, para nos salvar, Ele não deu um anjo ou pediu que um homem se tornasse o mártir, Ele deu o Seu Filho Unigênito, o Seu melhor, sem pecado. Então a excelência faz parte da ação do Espírito Santo de Deus" , disse.

A programação de inauguração teve início neste domingo (23) e segue por todo o mês de setembro.

articles.title: BYD mostra Mako para enfrentar Fiat Toro e VW Tukan. | G1
articles.standfirst: Picape híbrida plug-in chega em 2027 e será produzida em Camaçari. Protótipo mostrou suspensão confortável e autonomia total indicada de 977 km, mas ainda terá ajustes antes da versão definitiva.
articles.summary: Picape híbrida plug-in chega em 2027 e será produzida em Camaçari. Protótipo mostrou suspensão confortável e autonomia total indicada de 977 km.
articles.body:
BYD apresenta picape híbrida Mako — Foto: André Fogaça / g1

A BYD mostrou, nesta terça-feira (25), uma versão concluída da picape Mako. O modelo chegará ao Brasil no ano que vem para competir com Fiat Toro, Volkswagen Tukan e RAM Rampage e será fabricado em Camaçari (BA).

✅ Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 Carros no WhatsApp

A picape foi vista em detalhes pela primeira vez durante o Festival Interlagos, realizado no autódromo de Interlagos, em São Paulo. Um protótipo em estágio anterior de desenvolvimento já havia sido apresentado em um evento em Ribeirão Preto (SP) , no fim de abril deste ano.

O protótipo trazia um conjunto de suspensão semelhante ao usado no Song Pro, híbrido plug-in que está entre os cinco eletrificados mais vendidos do Brasil. A solução privilegia o conforto no uso urbano, mas pode limitar a capacidade de carga da picape.

Apesar de estar em um estágio mais avançado de desenvolvimento, o modelo exibido ainda é um protótipo e deve passar por mudanças até chegar às concessionárias.

A pintura final estava escondida sob adesivos que cobriam toda a carroceria;

Os dados técnicos ainda não estão definidos e podem mudar até o lançamento;

Alguns recursos estavam inoperantes, incluindo sistemas de assistência ao motorista, sensores de estacionamento e câmeras;

Parte do acabamento interno estava coberta, escondendo detalhes da versão final.

Pelas dimensões, a impressão é que a BYD Mako está mais próxima da proposta de uma Fiat Toro do que de picapes médias como Ford Ranger e Toyota Hilux. Ao mesmo tempo, tem porte superior ao da Fiat Strada.

Durante o teste, a direção pareceu excessivamente pesada, tanto em velocidades mais altas quanto nos trechos percorridos mais lentamente, como na área dos boxes.

BYD Mako no Festival Interlagos — Foto: André Fogaça/g1

A impressão era de que a assistência elétrica da direção não estava funcionando. Procurados, funcionários da BYD deram explicações diferentes sobre o comportamento: não ficou claro se ele é resultado da falta de calibração do protótipo ou se será mantido na versão de produção.

Se a direção desagradou, a suspensão causou a impressão oposta. Na parte inferior da Mako, o conjunto se mostrou semelhante ao utilizado no Song Pro.

Na pista, essa impressão se confirmou. A Mako apresentou um acerto voltado ao conforto urbano, sem oscilações excessivas da carroceria em acelerações bruscas, frenagens intensas e curvas em alta velocidade.

Embora realizado no autódromo que recebe a Fórmula 1, o teste buscou reproduzir condições de uso urbano. Nesse aspecto, a suspensão se mostrou bem ajustada e próxima do que se espera da versão final.

Na lateral, um segundo bocal confirmou que a picape utiliza um sistema híbrido plug-in, que permite recarregar a bateria em uma fonte externa. O painel não mostrava a autonomia exclusivamente elétrica, mas indicava 29% de carga na bateria e autonomia total de 977 km.

Com a bateria ainda carregada, o motor elétrico podia entregar toda a potência disponível. Nas acelerações, o desempenho lembrou o do BYD Song Pro já testado pelo g1 . A Mako acelera de forma contínua, combinando o motor 1.5 turbo com o propulsor elétrico.

No Song Pro, o conjunto entrega 219 cv de potência combinada e 30,6 kgfm de torque. Como a picape é projetada para carregar mais peso, a expectativa é que a configuração seja ajustada para entregar mais torque.

Mako pode tentar reverter desempenho fraco da Shark

Mesmo sem preço confirmado, as dimensões colocam a BYD Mako em um segmento diferente do ocupado pela Shark . A Mako é uma picape compacta, enquanto a Shark pertence à categoria das médias.

A Mako pode ter mais chances de ganhar espaço no mercado brasileiro do que a Shark, que registra vendas baixas mesmo após quase dois anos no país.

Segundo a Federação Nacional da Distribuição de Veículos Automotores (Fenabrave), 415 unidades zero km da Shark foram emplacadas entre janeiro e julho de 2026.

O volume equivale a apenas 1,5% das 26.732 unidades da Toyota Hilux emplacadas no mesmo período e a 10,5% das 3.921 unidades da GWM Poer P30 vendidas pela rival chinesa.

articles.title: Suspeito de matar o próprio pai é preso no interior do Ceará | G1
articles.standfirst: O crime teria ocorrido em meio a desentendimentos entre os dois, já que pai reprovava o suposto envolvimento do filho com a venda de drogas.
articles.summary: O crime teria ocorrido em meio a desentendimentos entre os dois, já que pai reprovava o suposto envolvimento do filho com a venda de drogas.
articles.body:
Um jovem de 19 anos foi preso, nesta terça-feira (25), suspeito de ter matado o próprio pai em Barbalha , na região do Cariri cearense. O crime ocorreu no dia 10 de abril deste ano.

O suspeito foi identificado como João Pedro Sousa Santos, conhecido como "Pedão". O pai dele era Roberto dos Santos, conhecido como “Zoca”, e tinha 50 anos.

✅ Clique e siga o canal do g1 Ceará no WhatsApp

Segundo apuração da TV Verdes Mares , o assassinato teria ocorrido em meio a desentendimentos entre os dois, pois o pai não aceitava o envolvimento do filho com a venda de drogas .

Na tarde desta terça, João Pedro foi alvo de um mandado de prisão preventiva e foi conduzido para a Delegacia de Polícia Civil de Barbalha. O suspeito segue agora à disposição da Justiça.

Suspeito foi conduzido à Delegacia de Polícia Civil de Barbalha — Foto: Reprodução

articles.title: Gangue mata 47 pessoas, sequestra outras 50 no Haiti | G1
articles.standfirst: Chefe de organização criminosa disse que vai matar todos os reféns se forças policiais avançarem. Sequestro em massa foi um dos maiores já registrados no país.
articles.summary: Chefe de organização criminosa disse que vai matar todos os reféns se forças policiais avançarem. Sequestro em massa foi um dos maiores já registrados no país.
articles.body:
Mulher chora perto de corpos de familiares que morreram em ataque de gangue no Haiti — Foto: AP Photo/Odelyn Joseph

Pelo menos 47 pessoas morreram e mais de 50 foram sequestradas depois que homens armados atacaram, no domingo (23), uma comunidade que era considerada tranquila nos arredores de Porto Príncipe, capital do Haiti , segundo a ONU. Entre os mortos estão cinco crianças.

✅ Siga o canal de notícias internacionais do g1 no WhatsApp

O ataque a Kenscoff é considerado um dos maiores sequestros em massa registrados no Haiti nos últimos anos. Um dos líderes de gangue ameaçou matar os reféns caso forças de segurança matem integrantes dos grupos criminosos durante as operações para retomar o controle da região.

O prefeito da cidade, Jean Massillon, disse à Associated Press que as gangues incendiaram 25 casas e mataram dois funcionários do governo. Um deles era primo do gestor e fazia parte da equipe responsável pela segurança dele.

A ofensiva também abalou a percepção de que a segurança no país caribenho vinha melhorando.

“Este é um grande teste político e de segurança para o governo, para a polícia e para a missão internacional”, disse Romain Le Cour, diretor do Observatório do Haiti, da Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime.

Segundo ele, a ameaça de execução dos reféns coloca as forças de segurança em uma armadilha. Caso não ajam, serão acusadas de não proteger as vítimas. Se avançarem e houver mortes, as gangues poderão responsabilizar o Estado.

Marc Paul, de 42 anos, morador de Kenscoff, disse que o irmão, a madrasta, o padrasto e dois primos foram sequestrados. Uma sobrinha de 16 anos também foi levada e estuprada, mas conseguiu escapar e reencontrou a família.

“Eu precisei correr sobre corpos”, disse Paul ao lembrar da fuga durante o ataque. “Não consigo dormir sabendo que todas essas pessoas morreram.”

A família já havia perdido a casa em outro ataque de gangues, em janeiro de 2025. Segundo Paul, porém, a violência naquela ocasião foi menor do que a registrada no domingo.

“Meu irmão provavelmente vai morrer”, disse ele, ao comentar um vídeo publicado pelas gangues.

Moradores do Haiti empurram carro destruído em protesto contra a insegurança, em 24 de agosto de 2026 — Foto: Fildor Pq Egeder/Reuters

Em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, um líder de gangue ameaçou Vladimir Paraison, diretor da Polícia Nacional do Haiti.

“Paraison, se algum dos nossos soldados for ferido, vou matar todos eles”, disse, referindo-se aos reféns.

O homem se identificou como Izo 2, em referência a Izo, ou Johnson André, um dos líderes de gangue mais poderosos do Haiti.

Le Cour disse que Izo 2 também é conhecido como “Didi” e comanda o grupo armado em Kenscoff em nome e em coordenação com Izo e outros líderes criminosos.

Kenson Paul, sobrinho de Marc Paul, de 17 anos, disse que conseguiu escapar dos criminosos.

“Eles ainda não nos ligaram para dizer o que querem”, afirmou, referindo-se aos sequestradores. “Tenho medo pela vida da minha família.”

Para Le Cour, o objetivo do ataque pode ter sido obrigar a polícia haitiana e a força de combate às gangues apoiada pela ONU a deslocar ainda mais os poucos recursos disponíveis.

“Eles não têm pessoal suficiente”, disse o especialista em entrevista por telefone. “Se você os força a enviar mais tropas, isso inevitavelmente será feito às custas de outras áreas.”

O ataque também pode ter sido uma demonstração de força e um recado ao governo e à polícia do Haiti, que se prepara para realizar eleições gerais em 13 de dezembro, pela primeira vez em mais de uma década.

“É uma mensagem ao governo e à polícia de que as promessas de proteção não correspondem à realidade”, disse Le Cour. “As gangues estão dizendo: quando decidimos atacar, podemos atacar, e vamos conseguir.”

Mulher chora ao lado de vítima de ataque de gangue no Haiti, em 24 de agosto de 2026 — Foto: Fildor Pq Egeder/Reuters

O primeiro grande ataque contra Kenscoff ocorreu em janeiro de 2025. Desde então, houve ofensivas esporádicas nas montanhas ao redor do centro da cidade. A ação de domingo, porém, foi a maior até agora.

O secretário-geral da ONU, António Guterres, condenou o ataque nesta terça-feira (25). Segundo ele, 22 das vítimas foram executadas em um complexo de uma igreja onde haviam buscado abrigo.

“Os ataques incessantes de gangues contra comunidades e a perda de vidas ressaltam as alarmantes condições de segurança no Haiti”, afirmou Guterres.

As gangues têm interesse em controlar Kenscoff porque a região permite cercar e controlar Pétion-Ville, uma área nobre da capital, além de rotas alternativas que ligam Porto Príncipe ao sul do país, segundo María Fernanda Arocha, pesquisadora da Armed Conflict Location & Event Data.

Entre janeiro e agosto deste ano, operações de segurança haviam conseguido reduzir a violência em Kenscoff em 66%, antes do ataque de domingo, afirmou Arocha.

Enquanto as forças de segurança concentravam esforços para recuperar o controle de áreas centrais de Porto Príncipe, os grupos criminosos passaram a tentar expandir a atuação para comunidades rurais vulneráveis pela baixa capacidade de resposta da polícia, mas que permanecem estratégicas, segundo a pesquisadora.

Protesto no Haiti após ataque de gangue, em 24 de agosto de 2026 — Foto: Fildor Pq Egeder/Reuters

Sobreviventes acusaram o governo de não ter oferecido proteção suficiente antes do ataque. A Polícia Nacional do Haiti negou as acusações.

Para Le Cour, caso policiais e veículos blindados realmente estivessem posicionados em Kenscoff antes da ofensiva, a situação gera preocupação.

“Você deixou as gangues entrarem mesmo tendo tudo preparado?”, questionou.

Homens armados controlam cerca de 70% de Porto Príncipe e grandes áreas da região central do Haiti e de outras partes do país.

A violência das gangues provocou o deslocamento de um número recorde de 1,5 milhão de pessoas no Haiti. Mais de 3.050 pessoas foram mortas entre janeiro e junho, segundo dados divulgados pela ONU na terça-feira.

A organização também informou que quase 800 estupros foram registrados entre abril e junho. Em 87% dos casos, as vítimas relataram estupros coletivos. No mesmo período, pelo menos 81 pessoas foram sequestradas, segundo um novo relatório da ONU.

“Esses números representam apenas uma parcela do total de pessoas sequestradas”, afirmou o documento.

“Em muitos casos, familiares das vítimas não comunicam os sequestros à polícia ou a prestadores de serviços e preferem negociar diretamente com os sequestradores, acreditando que essa abordagem permite uma libertação mais rápida e evita possíveis represálias.”

O número de sequestros registrados entre abril e junho foi mais de 40% maior do que no trimestre anterior.
paragraphs: Mulher chora perto de corpos de familiares que morreram em ataque de gangue no Haiti — Foto: AP Photo/Odelyn Joseph

Pelo menos 47 pessoas morreram e mais de 50 foram sequestradas depois que homens armados atacaram, no domingo (23), uma comunidade que era considerada tranquila nos arredores de Porto Príncipe, capital do Haiti , segundo a ONU. Entre os mortos estão cinco crianças.
✅ Siga o canal de notícias internacionais do g1 no WhatsApp

O ataque a Kenscoff é considerado um dos maiores sequestros em massa registrados no Haiti nos últimos anos. Um dos líderes de gangue ameaçou matar os reféns caso forças de segurança matem integrantes dos grupos criminosos durante as operações para retomar o controle da região.

O prefeito da cidade, Jean Massillon, disse à Associated Press que as gangues incendiaram 25 casas e mataram dois funcionários do governo. Um deles era primo do gestor e fazia parte da equipe responsável pela segurança dele.
A ofensiva também abalou a percepção de que a segurança no país caribenho vinha melhorando.

“Este é um grande teste político e de segurança para o governo, para a polícia e para a missão internacional”, disse Romain Le Cour, diretor do Observatório do Haiti, da Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime.

Segundo ele, a ameaça de execução dos reféns coloca as forças de segurança em uma armadilha. Caso não ajam, serão acusadas de não proteger as vítimas. Se avançarem e houver mortes, as gangues poderão responsabilizar o Estado.

“Meu irmão provavelmente vai morrer”, disse ele, ao comentar um vídeo publicado pelas gangues.

articles.title: Quaest: veja como está a disputa pelo governo de RO | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa divulgada nesta terça-feira (25) foi encomendada pela Rede Amazônica. Margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais.
articles.summary: Pesquisa divulgada nesta terça-feira (25) foi encomendada pela Rede Amazônica. Margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais.
articles.body:
Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta terça-feira (25) mostra como está a disputa pelo governo de Rondônia. O levantamento foi encomendado pela Rede Amazônica.

Veja, abaixo, os resultados da pesquisa estimulada, em que a Quaest mostra a lista de candidatos aos eleitores entrevistados.

Para 57% dos eleitores ouvidos no levantamento, a escolha do candidato é definitiva. Outros 42% dizem que ainda podem mudar o voto até as eleições, em 4 de outubro.

A Quaest ouviu 804 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais entre os dias 21 e 24 de agosto de 2026. A margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos, e o nível de confiança é de 95%. O levantamento foi registrado no TSE com os números RO-05711/2026 e BR-00490/2026.

Quaest para o Senado em Rondônia: Máximo, 17%; Cristina, 11%; Sheid, 11%; Mariana, 10%

Quaest em RO: 46% aprovam e 34% desaprovam governo de Marcos Rocha (PSD)

Quaest em Rondônia: Flávio Bolsonaro, 45%; Lula, 25%

A Quaest mostra também os resultados da pesquisa espontânea, em que os nomes dos candidatos não são mostrados aos eleitores.

A pesquisa traz seis simulações de 2º turno. Os dados estão abaixo:

17% dos eleitores dizem que o governador a ser eleito deve continuar o trabalho que vem sendo feito.

34% defendem mudar apenas o que não está bom

44% consideram que é necessário mudar totalmente

23% preferem que o governador eleito seja aliado de Lula

43% preferem um aliado de Flávio Bolsonaro

18% dizem que o apoio de Lula aumenta a chance de votar no candidato

43% dizem que diminui a chance de votar no candidato

36% dizem que o apoio de Flávio Bolsonaro aumenta a chance de votar no candidato

19% dizem que diminui a chance de votar no candidato

A Quaest perguntou aos eleitores qual é o principal problema do estado. Veja os temas mais citados.

A Quaest consultou também aos eleitores sobre cada um dos candidatos: se eles conhecem e votariam, se não conhecem ou se conhecem e não votariam. Os candidatos mais rejeitados (maiores índices de "conhece e não votaria") são Expedito Netto (PT) e Marcos Rogério (PL).

A pesquisa mostra também como está a avaliação do governo e os índices de aprovação e desaprovação.

Marcos Rocha merece ser reeleito ou merece eleger um sucessor?

Marcos Rogério; Adailton Furia; Expedito Netto; Hildon Chaves — Foto: Reprodução

articles.title: Mega-Sena pode pagar R$ 3.5 milhões nesta terça-feira; g1 transmite | G1
articles.standfirst: Apostas podem ser feitas até as 20h em lotéricas ou pela internet.
articles.summary: Apostas podem ser feitas até as 20h em lotéricas ou pela internet.
articles.body:
O concurso 3.049 da Mega-Sena pode pagar um prêmio de R$ 3,5 milhões para os apostadores que acertarem as seis dezenas. O sorteio ocorre às 21h desta terça-feira (25), em São Paulo.

📱Favorite o g1 no Google e acompanhe as principais notícias do dia

Clique aqui para seguir o canal de Loterias do g1 no WhatsApp

No concurso do último domingo (23) , uma aposta simples em Santa Catarina levou o prêmio de R$ 57 milhões.

O g1 transmite todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

Acompanhe os sorteios no canal do g1 no YouTube

A aposta mínima para a Mega-Sena custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Volante da Mega-Sena — Foto: Ana Marin/g1

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

Ainda segundo a Caixa, para os sorteios realizados aos domingos as apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado por meio das unidades lotéricas, pelo Portal Loterias Caixa e do aplicativo Loterias Caixa.

A comercialização dos Bolões Caixa nos canais eletrônicos, nesse caso, acontece até às 10h45 do domingo, quinze minutos antes da realização dos sorteios.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: João Campos promete centros TEA em todas as regiões de Pernambuco | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PSB ao governo de Pernambuco cumpriu agenda de campanha no bairro do Ibura, na Zona Sul do Recife, nesta terça (25).
articles.summary: Candidato do PSB ao governo de Pernambuco cumpriu agenda de campanha no bairro do Ibura, na Zona Sul do Recife, nesta terça (25).
articles.body:
O ex-prefeito do Recife João Campos , candidato a govenador pelo PSB , cumpriu agenda de campanha no bairro do Ibura, na Zona Sul do Recife, na manhã desta terça-feira (25). Ele visitou uma UPA Especialidades (UPAE) e prometeu, se eleito, criar centros de atendimento a pessoas com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA) em todas as regiões do estado ( veja vídeo acima ).

O candidato visitou a unidade, que fica na Avenida Dois Rios. Na chegada ao local, ele conversou com moradores e trabalhadores informais. João Campos visitou o centro TEA que funciona dentro da unidade.

✅ Receba no WhatsApp as notícias do g1 PE

O candidato do PSB conversou com profissionais de saúde que trabalham no local e com mães atípicas. Ele prometeu a criação de uma rede de centros TEA em todas as UPAs Especialidades de Pernambuco.
